newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Want to make a living? Try strangling your cat.
newsitem.headline: Want to make a living? Try strangling your cat.

text.p: If cat owners in the central Philippine city of Cebu are missing their pets, chances are they will find them in a slaughterhouse in Bangkal village -- strangled and skinned.
Workers at the slaughterhouse near Cebu said they kill about 300 cats a week and export their skins to Japan to be used for making guitars and drums, the weekly Freeman newspaper said on Tuesday.
The guitars and drums are sold to Taiwan and China, it said.
Workers carry out the slaughter twice a week, spending the other days buying cats from suppliers, including children who sell them at 20 pesos (76 U.S. cents) per feline, according to the Freeman.
Little was known about the trade until a local councillor last week broke the news about it after seeing children chasing cats in city streets, the Freeman said.
Slaughterhouse owner Gina Custodio denied her workers sell the cat meat for human consumption.
"We bury them (the skinned cat corpses) in the backyard," she told the Freeman.
